scope.description: Whole r application/library breadth across useful functional families.
scope.denominator: Statistical programming, data manipulation, model families/inference, visualisation, time series and extensible packages.

coverage.rationale: Explicit new-observation confidence and prediction intervals deepen the existing OLS calibration family. General statistical programming, data manipulation, other models and plotting remain absent, so the whole-application estimate remains 5%.

scope.description: Full-rank numeric OLS calibration with held-out predictions, coefficient uncertainty, named requirements and declared new-observation mean-response confidence or individual prediction intervals.
scope.denominator: User intent and domain decisions within the named supported workflows, including declared inputs, composition and useful outputs; excluded application features do not enter this score.

abstraction.rationale: Predictor units, calibration and inference intent, held-out acceptance requirements and explicit interval meaning hide formulas, fitting, reopen and interval plumbing. Users retain responsibility for the regression assumptions and scope; the existing 85% estimate remains within this OLS workflow family.

limitations: Small full-rank numeric OLS with explicit predictors; no categorical/missing data, interactions, weights, arbitrary formulas or general R programs. Intervals rely on the stated linear, independent, normal and homoscedastic error assumptions.

Mean-response confidence and individual future-observation intervals have different meanings. Neither establishes model validity, causality, future generalisation or empirical coverage; extrapolation is labelled rather than certified.

Rows whose interval types cannot be distinguished within the actual verification allowance are refused before native work. Eight-predictor interval tables exceed the bounded Gnuplot consumer column limit.

Subjective source-contract assessment, not an exhaustive native API measurement. Live lifecycle evidence is stage bounded, with no claim about the instruction position inside predict.lm; qualification and runtime availability remain separate.
